CORRECTION — this is Lane D scope, not a stray defect.

Design v2 §3.3 declares ServeSpawned as part of the business lane:

  // ServeSpawned is the child half: it claims fd 3 (ClaimHandoff's structural
  // check ...), adopts the session limits the parent conveyed alongside the
  // nonce, echoes the nonce, and serves exactly one session ...
  func ServeSpawned(ctx context.Context, contract Contract, handle Handler) error

and directive D8(ii) names "the ClaimHandoff/ServeSpawned double-claim" as one of the three
required named refusals. So childside.go:38's godoc and claimSpawnedHandoff's "both child-side
entry points" are forward-looking scaffold written against the design, not stale text — Lane C
built the claim helper with Lane D's second caller in mind.

The gap is therefore real but unowned rather than wrong: the conveyance has no consumer until
ServeSpawned exists. Lane D closes it by construction — ServeSpawned adopts the conveyed limits,
echoes the nonce, and refuses a contract whose limits disagree.

Acceptance criteria stand, but they are Lane D's exit criteria now, not an independent fix.
